jobs.title: Research Staff, Voice AI Foundations - Remote
jobs.description:
Company Overview 
 Deepgram is the leading platform underpinning the emerging trillion-dollar Voice AI economy, providing real-time APIs for speech-to-text (STT), text-to-speech (TTS), and building production-grade voice agents at scale. More than 200,000 developers and 1,300+ organizations build voice offerings that are ‘Powered by Deepgram’, including Twilio, Cloudflare, Sierra, Decagon, Vapi, Daily, Cresta, Granola, and Jack in the Box. Deepgram’s voice-native foundation models are accessed through cloud APIs or as self-hosted and on-premises software, with unmatched accuracy, low latency, and cost efficiency. Backed by a recent Series C led by leading global investors and strategic partners, Deepgram has processed over 50,000 years of audio and transcribed more than 1 trillion words. There is no organization in the world that understands voice better than Deepgram.

 Company Operating Rhythm 
 At Deepgram, we expect an AI-first mindset—AI use and comfort aren’t optional, they’re core to how we operate, innovate, and measure performance.
 Every team member who works at Deepgram is expected to actively use and experiment with advanced AI tools, and even build your own into your everyday work. We measure how effectively AI is applied to deliver results, and consistent, creative use of the latest AI capabilities is key to success here. Candidates should be comfortable adopting new models and modes quickly, integrating AI into their workflows, and continuously pushing the boundaries of what these technologies can do.
 Additionally, we move at the pace of AI. Change is rapid, and you can expect your day-to-day work to evolve just as quickly. This may not be the right role if you’re not excited to experiment, adapt, think on your feet, and learn constantly, or if you’re seeking something highly prescriptive with a traditional 9-to-5.

 The Opportunity
 Voice is the most natural modality for human interaction with machines. However, current sequence modeling paradigms based on jointly scaling model and data cannot deliver voice AI capable of universal human interaction. The challenges are rooted in fundamental data problems posed by audio: real-world audio data is scarce and enormously diverse, spanning a vast space of voices, speaking styles, and acoustic conditions. Even if billions of hours of audio were accessible, its inherent high dimensionality creates computational and storage costs that make training and deployment prohibitively expensive at world scale. We believe that entirely new paradigms for audio AI are needed to overcome these challenges and make voice interaction accessible to everyone.

The Role
 As a Member of the Research Staff, you will pioneer the development of Latent Space Models (LSMs), a new approach that aims to solve the fundamental data, scale, and cost challenges associated with building robust, contextualized voice AI. Your research will focus on solving one or more of the following problems:

 Build next-generation neural audio codecs that achieve extreme, low bit-rate compression and high fidelity reconstruction across a world-scale corpus of general audio.

 Pioneer steerable generative models that can synthesize the full diversity of human speech from the codec latent representation, from casual conversation to highly emotional expression to complex multi-speaker scenarios with environmental noise and overlapping speech.

 Develop embedding systems that cleanly factorize the codec latent space into interpretable dimensions of speaker, content, style, environment, and channel effects -- enabling precise control over each aspect and the ability to massively amplify an existing seed dataset through “latent recombination”.

 Leverage latent recombination to generate synthetic audio data at previously impossible scales, unlocking joint model and data scaling paradigms for audio.  Endeavor to train multimodal speech-to-speech systems that can 1) understand any human irrespective of their demographics,

jobs.title: AI Research Engineer (Agentic Reinforcement Learning)
jobs.description:
This position is listed on behalf of a partner company, who manages all applications and next steps. Our partner is looking for an AI Research Engineer (Agentic Reinforcement Learning) based in Netherlands. 

 As an AI Research Engineer specializing in Agentic Reinforcement Learning, you will drive research and innovation in next-generation intelligent systems.
You will develop advanced reinforcement learning techniques that improve decision-making, adaptive behavior, and performance across multimodal AI architectures.
Working with text, images, audio, and other data modalities, you will help build models capable of solving complex, real-world challenges.
Your work will involve designing scalable training infrastructure, optimizing reward mechanisms, and improving the reliability of autonomous AI agents.
You will explore cutting-edge approaches involving diffusion-based generative models, autoregressive architectures, and unified multimodal frameworks.
Through rigorous experimentation and benchmarking, you will push the boundaries of model performance, efficiency, and generalization.
This fully remote opportunity offers the chance to contribute to impactful AI research within a fast-moving, globally distributed technology environment.

 Accountabilities 

 In this role, you will conduct advanced research and develop scalable reinforcement learning systems for multimodal AI applications. Your main responsibilities will include:

 Research and develop reinforcement learning algorithms for multimodal models, including diffusion-based approaches for image generation, autoregressive models for multimodal understanding, and unified architectures integrating multiple modalities.

 Design and implement scalable reinforcement learning infrastructure supporting distributed training across complex multimodal systems.

 Develop and optimize reward modeling strategies to improve training stability, align model behavior with desired outcomes, and prevent reward hacking and related failure modes.

 Create, curate, and maintain multimodal simulation environments and training datasets to support robust model development, evaluation, and benchmarking.

 Design and implement rigorous evaluation protocols to measure model performance, monitor progress against established baselines, and validate research improvements.

 Analyze and optimize policy performance across different modalities by identifying bottlenecks in training, credit assignment, reward optimization, and cross-modal alignment.

 Investigate emerging reinforcement learning paradigms that enable AI agents to learn more effectively from environmental feedback.

 Improve model exploration, decision-making, and adaptive behavior to achieve state-of-the-art performance in dynamic, real-world environments.

 Conduct large-scale experiments and translate empirical findings into practical algorithmic improvements.

 Publish and present research findings at leading international conferences, including ICML, NeurIPS, ICLR, CVPR, ICCV, and ECCV.

 Requirements 

 The ideal candidate combines strong theoretical knowledge of reinforcement learning with hands-on experience developing and optimizing large-scale multimodal AI systems. The following qualifications and technical skills are expected:

 Master's degree in Computer Science or a related discipline. A PhD in Machine Learning, Natural Language Processing, Computer Vision, or a closely related field is preferred.

 Strong track record of AI research, including publications in leading international conferences.

 Demonstrated experience conducting large-scale reinforcement learning experiments in multimodal and vision-centric systems, including online reinforcement learning environments.

 Proven ability to improve domain-specific decision-making and achieve measurable gains in policy performance.

 Deep understanding of reinforcement learning algorithms and optimization techniques applied to vision and multimodal learning.

 Strong knowledge

jobs.title: Senior Machine Learning Engineer
jobs.description:
Imagine building intelligent systems that don’t just work in perfect lab conditions, but 
 perform reliably in the real world, where uncertainty is the norm and failure is not an 
 option. As a Machine Learning Engineer, you will push the limits of computer vision by 
 designing, training, and validating neural networks that operate in complex, safety-critical 
 environments. Your work will directly influence how autonomous systems perceive and 
 interact with the world, combining deep learning, simulation, and rigorous verification into 
 one seamless pipeline.
 At Destinus, we are shaping the future of defense through high-speed, autonomous flight 
 technologies. We develop next-generation unmanned aerial systems that deliver greater 
 speed, precision, and efficiency, supporting governments and defense organizations in 
 mission-critical operations worldwide. Daedalean AG, the AI and autonomy hub of the 
 Destinus Group, plays a key role in this vision. Developing safety-critical AI systems at the 
 intersection of advanced research and real-world aviation. Enabling machines to perceive, 
 understand, and make decisions in real time. Together, we combine aerospace 
 engineering and artificial intelligence to build the next generation of autonomous flight 
 systems, driving innovation where it matters most.

 What You´ll Do 
 • Design, train, and optimize deep learning models for computer vision tasks in highly 
 dynamic and safety-critical environments 
 • Manage the development lifecycle of ML capabilities, from early-stage data 
 collection to the operational deployments of mature systems
 • Develop robust evaluation pipelines to ensure models meet strict reliability and 
 safety requirements 
 • Leverage transfer learning and simulation to scale training and testing beyond realworld data limitations 
 • Collaborate closely with software, systems, and flight teams to integrate ML models 
 into real-world applications
 • Continuously push model performance across edge cases, environmental 
 variability, and operational constraints

 Requirements 
 Strong programming skills in C++ or Rust
 • At least 5 years of hands-on experience in deep learning for computer vision 
 • Experience across the full ML stack, including model design, distributed training 
 frameworks, evaluation pipelines and resource-constrained inference platforms
 • Experience with simulation environments or synthetic data generation is a strong 
 plus 
 • Experience with working with integrated sensors, including infrared cameras
 • Master’s degree or PhD in computer science, physics, mathematics, or a related 
 technical field- or equal proven practical experience
